# Draft: refund agent, note to Sam Lind

For Dana Okafor, written 4 January 2027. Draft only. Nothing has been sent.

## For you first

AI BVF now returns Accelerate for the customer service agent. On 23 November it returned Fix. An agent answered these questions from evidence it quoted. No person has confirmed the answers.

What moved it is in the steering minutes of 10 December: "The refund limits are now written into the service policy: 50 euros per order and 500 euros per customer per month. Dana Okafor approves any refund above the limits and can switch the agent off. Signed off on 2 December."

One caveat. The tool asks what was redesigned before go-live. The team's measures changed after it.

- 10 November: "The team's measures stay as they are for now. Handling time per contact remains the main target." (process design)
- 9 December: "The agent went live for all first-line queries on 9 December." (steering minutes, 10 December)
- 10 December: "From January the returns team is measured on first response time and on reversed refunds. Handling time per contact is dropped as a target." (steering minutes, 10 December)

I answered that all four parts of the work are redesigned as of today. I found no January record of the new measures in use. If handling time is still a target, tell me and I will judge again with your words.

The note below asks Sam for what the next review needs.

## The note

- To: Sam Lind
- Cc: Mira Aalto, Piet Hauer
- From: Dana Okafor
- Subject: Refund agent: go ahead, and what the 15 February review needs

Sam,

My AI BVF agent judged the refund agent again on 4 January. The verdict moved from Fix to Accelerate.

An agent answered the questions from our documents. No person has confirmed the answers.

The first step it returned: "Go ahead, and answer the same questions again at the first review."

That review is on 15 February. Please file three things before then.

1. The January results, set out like your first-month note: contacts resolved against plan, first response under two minutes, measured saving against monthly cost.
2. A record that the returns team is now measured on first response time and on reversed refunds.
3. Any change to the refund limits, or to who approves above them and can switch the agent off.

Dana
